solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, mirror symmetry); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Risk needing a sling?

parts.note: the idiom for taking a gamble is read literally as hazarding a limb so badly that it ends up strapped in a sling

explanation.surface: A daredevil weighs up a gamble that could leave them with an injured limb.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for taking a chance is pictured literally: risk a limb and you may need a sling for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to attempt something risky in the hope of success.

clue.text: Hit copper with repeated force

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: repeated tells us to write the force abbreviation twice over

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A policeman lashes out, striking again and again with force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a light blow with the open hand, as in a clip round the ear.

clue.text: One sent out letters covered in beer

indicators.note: the letters are wrapped round, covered, by the beer word

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
post means mail, letters delivered

explanation.surface: Someone's mail has got soaked in spilt beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek root means 'one sent forth', which is why the disciples sent out to preach bear the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A messenger dispatched to spread a teaching, like the twelve sent by Jesus.

clue.text: Country engaged in machinations?

indicators.note: the word sits caught up inside the letters of machinations

explanation.surface: A nation is involved in political scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in East Asia, the world's most populous until recently.

clue.text: Work on it ineptly for choice

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: done ineptly, the letters of on it are jumbled clumsily

explanation.surface: Someone tinkers clumsily with a project because they choose to.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an alternative one may select, something chosen.

clue.text: Clue "Seascape" with an anagram? It's a potential way out

indicators.note: the clue openly tells the solver to rearrange the two words before it

explanation.surface: A setter muses on cluing a word with an anagram, then hints at an exit.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: it really is an anagram clue for the letters of CLUE SEASCAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract provision allowing a party to withdraw from obligations under set conditions.

clue.text: A type of grain I ditched in shock

indicators.note: ditched means thrown out, so the letter I is dropped

parts.note: maize is a cereal grain, corn

explanation.surface: Someone throws away a kind of cereal in alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to astonish or stun someone greatly.

clue.text: Awful aching torment that needle points to

indicators.note: awful suggests something messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient describes the terrible pain a needle causes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needle' suggests an injection; it is a compass needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass needle aligns with the earth's magnetic field, pointing to this polar spot.

clue.text: Exclamation when probing handwriting — blooming shopkeeper!

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so the exclamation goes into the handwriting word

parts.note: fist is an informal word for someone's handwriting
lor is a dialect exclamation of surprise, a form of Lord!

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims while examining a scrawl, then insults a shopkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' reads as a mild British curse but describes the flowers sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who sells flowers, the blooms in the shop.

clue.text: Family group's beginning a racket

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of group's is taken

explanation.surface: A family band starts up a terrible din.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud metallic noise, a din.

clue.text: Elevated position in Mad Hatter's prose

indicators.note: mad means crazy, telling us to scramble the letters

explanation.surface: A lofty passage appears in writing by Alice in Wonderland's Mad Hatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad Hatter' looks like the character, but Mad is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of the atmosphere high above the earth, figuratively a very high level.

clue.text: Someone getting a buzz from their hobby?

definitions.text: Someone getting a buzz from their hobby?

parts.words: Someone getting a buzz from their hobby?
parts.note: a buzz means a thrill but also literal humming, as from hives of bees kept as a pastime

explanation.surface: A description of an enthusiast who loves their pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper, whose hobby literally buzzes.

clue.text: Bound to return to US city for the Spanish food

indicators.note: to return means the jump word is read backwards

parts.note: a bound is a leap
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone is set to fly back to an American city for Spanish cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice dish from Valencia, cooked with saffron, seafood or meat.

clue.text: Seriously inaccurate stories about artist making free

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the artist goes inside

parts.note: libel is damaging false published statement
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Damaging tales told about a painter are being spread freely.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: generous, given freely and in plenty, as in liberal helpings.

clue.text: Sea creatures affected during island's revolution

indicators.note: during means within, so this goes inside
a revolution turns the island letters round

parts.note: I for island plus S from the apostrophe s
camp means theatrically affected

explanation.surface: Marine life is disturbed while an island undergoes a political upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: Langoustines, Norway lobsters, often served breaded.

clue.text: Argue about Northern Line, one not seen in the brightest light

definitions.text: not seen in the brightest light

indicators.note: about means around, so the argue word encloses the rest

parts.note: to moot is to raise or argue a point
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Commuters argue about a London Tube line where someone vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern Line' reads as the London Underground line, but splits into N and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit by the moon only, a dimmer glow than daylight or sunshine.

clue.text: Nothing overlooked in keeping yarn

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so the zero is dropped

parts.note: storing means keeping
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: No thought is given to storing wool.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: thread or twine, a length of spun fibre.

clue.text: A man from the Balkans secures British circus performer

indicators.note: secures means holds tight inside

parts.note: a Croat is from Croatia in the Balkans

explanation.surface: A Balkan man hires a British big-top artiste.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast performing tumbling and trapeze feats in a circus.

clue.text: Search thoroughly for weapon

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb meaning ransack and a noun for a long gun.

clue.text: A scam to snaffle farmer's last fruit from tree

indicators.note: snaffle means seize, so the con word takes in a letter

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of farmer's, ignoring the apostrophe s

explanation.surface: A swindler grabs the farmer's final crop from the orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the oak, its seed-bearing fruit.

clue.text: Deduce no escaping from fire

indicators.note: escaping suggests letters breaking free and scattering

parts.note: N is short for no, as in Y/N

explanation.surface: Someone concludes there is no way out of the blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to conclude by reasoning from evidence.

clue.text: Keeping to oneself, sulk endlessly amidst dreadful rain

indicators.note: amidst means in the middle of, so the sulking letters go inside
dreadful signals the letters of rain are messed up
endlessly drops the final letter of sulk

explanation.surface: A loner sulks through miserable rainy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' makes SUL and 'dreadful' turns rain into INAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Inward-looking and detached, like an island cut off from others.

clue.text: Those people will collect old record for religious study

indicators.note: collect means gather inside, so they encloses the rest

parts.note: they means those people
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A group will pick up an ancient document for divinity classes.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic study of God and religious belief, as at divinity school.

clue.text: Longing to thumb a lift in part of London?

indicators.note: Cockneys of East London drop their initial h sounds

parts.note: to hitch is to hitchhike

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to hitchhike somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, of London's East End, drops the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a restless craving, an urge.
